findings.title: 4/5/6 and 1/2/3 cannot share today's freqTo: the keyboard maps Digit3-5 to frequencies whatever the class
findings.claim: §9 says FREQ_CODES is read only on a laser class, and that a new GUN_FREQ_CODES (Digit4→0, Digit5→1, Digit6→2) feeds the same freqTo. The keyboard does not know the class. On every keydown in FREQ_CODES it sets freqTo (Digit3→0, Digit4→1, Digit5→2). One freqTo value cannot mean B on the laser fit and A on the Hound for the same key. On the Hound as written: pressing 3 to select the torpedo also sends laserFrequency A, which is now admitted. Pressing 4 sends B, not A. Selection digits also have no KeySample field to travel in.
findings.evidence: spec L463-466, L481-482; src/renderer/src/app/duel/input.ts:L21 (FREQ_CODES), L146 (`if (!e.repeat && FREQ_CODES[e.code] !== undefined) freqTo = ...`, class-agnostic); runtime.ts:L521-522 and onlineDuel.ts:L303 send laserFrequency from k.freqTo at the Weapons seat; step.ts:L387 (the admission the spec opens to the Hound).
findings.why: Two implementers would solve this differently (a class-aware keyboard, a second field, or raw codes). The obvious literal reading makes 3 both select the torpedo and retune the guns, a bug hit in ordinary play.
findings.fix: Specify the interface. Either the keyboard records the raw digit (e.g. `freqKey?: 'Digit3'|'Digit4'|'Digit5'|'Digit6'`) plus a `selectTo?: 0|1|2` from WEAPON_SELECT_CODES, and the runtime and online `play` map them by class; or the keyboard keeps two fields (`freqTo` from FREQ_CODES, `gunFreqTo` from GUN_FREQ_CODES) and the modes read one by class. Console frequency buttons keep writing freqTo directly. Add a w4Input test that 3 on the Hound queues no laserFrequency.

findings.title: The beam's leaving breaks a large set of Hound-laser tests the spec doesn't name, and §13.4's premise about manualLaser* is false
findings.claim: §13.4 says W-2's tests/manualLaser*.test.ts run on VALKYRN_LASER_CLASS and pass. They don't run on that class. Every one builds the Cutter: createTacticalState(5) with the default DUEL_CLASSES, parseShip(cutter), or createSeatedDuel(CUTTER). The laser fit ships only on the Valkyrn layout's Flight seat (main.ts L132, fleet.ts L22). That seat's runtime branch has no laserMode or laserFire path, so W-2's app tests (manualLaserInput, manualLaserScene, manualLaserUi) have no shipping seat to move to. More broadly, 56 test files send laser commands or read laserReleases or WeaponSlot.Beam. The helper todaysCrewWeapons puts 2 bars on WeaponSlot.Beam, which on the Hound now silently powers the autocannon. duelScripted's gunnerPew tests ('defence first', the spacing test) pin behaviour that no class keeps, since the Valkyrn has no pew. §14 lists none of these.
findings.evidence: spec L642-643, L580-581, L745-747; tests/manualLaserMode.test.ts:L18, manualLaserBeam.test.ts:L26, manualLaserInput.test.ts:L21, manualLaserUi.test.tsx:L77; tests/helpers/crewWeapons.ts:L9-13; tests/duelScripted.test.ts:L118-160; runtime.ts:L434-464 (Flight branch: no laserMode or laserFire); main.ts:L132; Grep: 300 laser-command occurrences across 56 test files (ftlTargeting 28, tacticalWeapons 25, onlineDuelSession 20, tacticalMissiles 16, duel 16, tacticalHunter 14, engManualBars 14, disabledSystems 14, ...).
findings.why: The plan's subagents will hit hundreds of red tests with no rule for each kind: port, replace or delete. The manualLaser 'passes unchanged' check, and with it the laser-fit fence, can't be met as written.
findings.fix: Add a §14 rule and an inventory. Sim tests that need a crew beam build state with cls ShipClass.ValkyrnLaser (createTacticalState or createDuel's cls argument). App tests for W-2 run the cutter layout with deps.cls = ValkyrnLaser, and the spec states that the laser-class Weapons-seat path is kept for that developer combination. todaysCrewWeapons is ported to the laser fit, with a sibling helper for the Hound. The gunnerPew tests are listed as kind (a) removals. List each affected file under kind a, b or port.

findings.title: W-4a's and W-4b's intermediate states are undefined: the gates, goldens and the pew's mode before AUTO exists
findings.claim: W-4a ships the gunner (spare bar to the autocannon, no pewFire, no laser) but no AUTO. So from W-4a to W-4b the crew bots fire no gun, and the per-seed gate `pewShots + gunShots ≥ 1` fails on every seed. Every rule change from W-4a on also moves tests/golden/duel-1.json, duel-rematch and the determinism fixture, but the bless is defined only at the merge (§13.3). W-4a's pewFire admission ('unavailable in AUTO') and pewGain's MAN table read gunsManual, which §3.1 places in W-4b. Each part still gets an 'Automated box' in docs/gates.md and is reviewed in turn.
findings.evidence: spec L856-870 (W-4a builds the gunner; 'the gates are judged at the merge'), L339-347 and L232 (AUTO-dependent rules), L104-108 (gunsManual is W-4b's state), L617-626 (bless only at the merge), L745-747.
findings.why: Each part must build and test cleanly in order. Without a rule, one plan leaves red tests on the branch, another skips them, and a third keeps the old gunner. Reviews of W-4a and W-4b can't tell regressions from expected failures.
findings.fix: State per part: (1) W-4a has no mode, so pewFire is admitted as MAN is later, with AUTO gain tables, and gunHeld fires the autocannon. (2) Either re-bless at SIM 59 on the branch at the end of each part (kind b), or name the tests marked `it.skip('until W-4b: …')` (the duelGates and duelScripted per-seed 'uses both weapons', the goldens), with W-4b's plan un-skipping them. (3) Alternatively keep W-4a's gunner sending a MAN pewFire until W-4b. Pick one.

findings.title: Online turret prediction (§11) can't be built as written and its test is vacuous
findings.claim: The spec says the client runs slewTurret 'over the held frames it has sent and the replica hasn't shown'. The client keeps no per-frame history: source.sent stores only the latest held, and unacked is a count capped at 30. slewTurret needs a heading per tick, but the Helm is the other player and its heading is not predicted. It also needs the mode (the replica's gunsManual or gunModeSent?) and the gates the sim applies (0 bars, a MANUAL torpedo in flight, unattended, the torpedo selected). The unacked count is in held frames, not ticks, and frames come faster than 60 Hz. The listed test, 'the predicted turret matches the stepped turret once the replica catches up', holds trivially at zero unacked frames.
findings.evidence: spec L543-550, L736-739; onlineSource.ts:L165-173 (thrMille = rampTicks(latest held, unackedFrames)), L208 (sent keeps the last held only); onlineDuel.ts:L393-399 (unacked from heldHighWater, UNACKED_MAX 30, L64).
findings.why: Two implementers would predict differently: a history buffer, or the latest aim repeated; replica or interpolated heading. Neither the agreement with the authority nor the behaviour on a mode change is testable as specified.
findings.fix: Define it as the throttle's analogue. predicted = slewTurret applied k = unacked times to the replica's turret, with the latest sent turretAim and the replica's heading. Traverse is MAN's when (gunModeSent?.manual ?? replica gunsManual) is true, and k = 0 when AUTO, bars 0, the torpedo selected or a MANUAL torpedo flying. Test: with unacked = k, a fixed heading and the same held, the prediction equals the authority's turret after k stepped ticks; a mode toggle in flight uses gunModeSent.

findings.title: The gates read pewShots/gunShots that the telemetry and DuelRun don't carry
findings.claim: §2.1 says the gates read pewShots and gunShots, and §14 kind (a) says the per-seed gate becomes `pewShots + gunShots ≥ 1`. ShipTelemetry has neither field. DuelRun keeps only telemetry and hashes, not the final systems. The Valkyrn gate gets gunShots from its own ValkyrnRun helper.
findings.evidence: spec L97-98, L745-747; sim/duel/telemetry.ts:L25-32 (ShipTelemetry fields); tests/helpers/scriptedDuel.ts:L30 (DuelRun); tests/helpers/valkyrnGate.ts:L23, L39 (gunShots read from systems).
findings.why: An interface the spec assumes doesn't exist. One implementer would add it to telemetry and another to the test helper.
findings.fix: Say where they come from: add `pewShots` and `gunShots` to DuelRun from the final `systems[0]` (as ValkyrnRun does), or to ShipTelemetry. Add them to telemetryLine for the report, with the hold-end tick and cause.

findings.title: Scripted gunner: the 'refused shipPower' case and the every-command-admitted test
findings.claim: The gunner sends shipPower and weaponPower in one tick, so it can't see a refused shipPower before weaponPower is judged. 'If the shipPower is refused, it moves nothing' only holds if the gunner checks for a spare bar and capacity before sending. duelScripted's whole-duel test requires every command 'applied' and pins the kinds list ['laserLock','sit','stand','torpLock','weaponPower']. On the Hound that list becomes shipPower without laserLock. Neither change is named.
findings.evidence: spec L559-564, L740-744; sim/duel/scripted.ts:L336-338 (barMoved gate); tests/duelScripted.test.ts:L88-95; sim/duel/power.ts:L41, L48-51 (sparesOf, applyPower refusals).
findings.why: A gunner that sends blindly fails the admitted-commands test whenever the spare is gone, and the pinned kinds list breaks without a named kind-(a) change.
findings.fix: Specify `moving = !barMoved && sparesOf(d) ≥ 1 && capacityOf(d, Weapons) > bars[Weapons] && weaponBars(Autocannon) === 0` on a turret class; otherwise send nothing. List the kinds-test update (shipPower in, laserLock out) under kind (a).

findings.title: Planet-vs-rock ties: the spec's 'as today' is the reverse of the code
findings.claim: §5.1 says the planet and a ship still win their ties over a rock, and §14 tests 'the planet and a ship keep their ties over a rock'. In stepRounds, rocks are swept before the planet and the planet needs a strictly smaller entry, so a rock wins an exact tie with the planet. The function's own doc says 'ship, then rocks by ascending slot, then the planet'.
findings.evidence: spec L282, L669; sim/tactical/gun.ts:L115 (doc), L134-140 (rock `t < best`, then planet `tp < best`).
findings.why: On the Hound a tie now decides whether a rock is worn. A test written from the spec fails, or the code gets changed to match the spec. Harmless for the Valkyrn, where both are absorbed, but it is a contradiction.
findings.fix: Write: 'a ship wins its ties; on an exact rock–planet tie the rock is the contact, as today', and test that.

findings.title: Tuning ladder has no step sizes, bounds or stop rule
findings.claim: The ladder names four knobs in order 'until the crew wins at least one seed'. It gives no direction or step (hitsPerHull 12→?), no limits, no rule for when to move to the next rung, and no outcome if all four fail. The target is also ungated, because the aggregate stays it.skip. The bots lose 10/10 today and now lose the beam's opener.
findings.why: Tuning can't be executed reproducibly by a subagent. Two runs would ship different AUTOCANNON numbers into SIM 60's goldens.
findings.fix: Give each rung its values (e.g. hitsPerHull 12, 10, 8, 6; AUTOCANNON_AUTO_RANGE 600 then 450; MISSILE_GAP −25 % steps; gunner bars 1/1/1 then 1/2/0). Say to stop at the first setting where at least one seed is a crew win and all per-seed gates pass. If none does, ship the base numbers and record the sweep in the report.

findings.title: Valkyrn identity 'leave out by name' and hunter.ts's ShipInput literal need stating
findings.claim: valkyrnIdentity digests the whole flattenTactical array. thrMille is left out only because it was never in it, so 'as it already leaves out thrMille' is no precedent. Dropping systems.*.pewTurret/gunTurret/gunsManual means rebuilding the array from the module fields and skipping those names. Separately, hunter.ts builds its own ShipInput literal with torpTurn, which must change even though §1 says hunter.ts keeps its code paths.
findings.why: These are small, but both are typecheck or digest traps for a fresh subagent.
findings.fix: Say the digest flattens via TACTICAL_MODULES' fields and skips the three names. Name hunter.ts:L143's literal in §8's ShipInput change (drop torpTurn; add turretAim −1, weaponSel −1, pewTrigger false).

verified: The gunner's +1/+1 reaches 1/1/1: START_BARS [2,2,3,1,1] uses 9 of REACTOR_BARS 10, Weapons is index 1 with 2 bars against START_WEAPON_POWER [1,0,1] (bars.ts:L8, L20-21, L70). Ship commands are admitted before weaponPower in the same tick (step.ts:L416-440).

Hostility counts shots + gunShots + pewShots or missilesLaunched, and hostilityStep runs after tickWeapons (science.ts:L36-42; duel.ts:L47-48). So AUTO opens on the tick after the hold ends, as §4.3 says.
Laser commands are 'unavailable' on a null laser (step.ts:L313). laserFrequency's admission is at step.ts:L387 and laserFrequency sits in the science module's command list (hash.ts:L179).

The Valkyrn's scripted gunner never sends pewFire, because gunnerPew returns when pewReady is false without a pew (scripted.ts:L311). Dropping pewFire's aim therefore can't change the Valkyrn pair's commands. The Hunter never sends pewFire; its pewAim path is separate (weapons.ts:L338; hunter.ts:L143).
hunterThink reads only the crew's rooms (hunter.ts:L164), so the Hound's class change doesn't move hunterThink's outputs for a fixed trajectory.
gunHit compares ++gunWear with the owner's threshold of the moment (gun.ts:L97). The gunWear bound most(hitsPerLayer) − 1 = 7 (hash.ts:L246) holds with a weak threshold of 4.
The gunCooldown bound is most(intervalTicks) (hash.ts:L245). AUTOCANNON spreads GUN (intervalTicks 6), so the explicit table term in spec L603 is needed and correct at 10.

Rock rules: rockHp = ceil(r/10), so r 15 gives 2 hp and 8 rounds at 0.25. hitRock pushes the hit event, bumps rockHits and fan-breaks at hp ≤ 0 with rocksBroken for the owner. pushRock wakes the rock and skips born pieces (rockBreak.ts:L54-74, L99-103; rocks.ts:L29, L33).

rockSounds plays ROCK_CRACK only for a 'laser' hit, so a 'gun' hit is silent by default (rockSounds.ts:L23). rockFx's spark is drawn only for collision bumps, so the 'gun' hit branch must be added (rockFx.ts:L51).

Held frames go out every frame (onlineDuel.ts:L393), so the 250 ms expiry only fires on a stalled link. neutralizeExpired writes NO_HELD (core.ts:L319-322), which clears turretAim, weaponSel and gunHeld together. The pause clear is at core.ts:L436.

Traverse arithmetic: 364, 455, 273 and 341 fine steps a tick at 60 Hz are 120.0°, 150.0°, 90.0° and 112.4°/s. AUTOCANNON_ARC_STEPS = floor(65536/12) = 5461. AUTO pew gains 360/60, 360/45, 360/30 and 360/24 = 6, 8, 12 and 15.
launchMissile sets torpRoom from torpLock and clears it; MANUAL takes no lock (missiles.ts:L21-35). manualTorpTurn's turn argument is separable from holdTurn (manualTorpedo.ts:L10-14).
pewFire's codec schema (codec.ts:L127), the held schema with torpTurn (codec.ts:L163-165) and HeldInput (contracts.ts:L40) are where §8 says. WEAPON_ORDER and DUEL_KINDS are at step.ts:L43-46.
